items.title: Abe Most interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: I have the Leonard Feather book from the 60s.

ctx.x: Yeah, that’s what I’m feeling. It might or might not work.

I read this strangest little anecdote in the — I have the Leonard Feather book from the 60s. I’ve never seen a little piece like this. In one sentence it said about you, it said, “Uses plastic reeds when playing jazz.” I said what a funny thing to put in there.

Well you know, Artie Shaw used plastic for a long time. And I didn’t — at one stage I didn’t care who knew it. As a matter of face since about twenty years ago, Arnold Brillhart made a reed for me which was made out of synthetic. I don’t like to call it plastic because it’s a little kinder. So I use it. And everybody since has asked me where they can get them. Because I get my own clarinet sound and it’s clarinet, but I hate to look for cane reeds.
